Track transition entropy over time in sliding windows

Source: R/transition_entropy.R
entropy_trajectory.Rd

entropy_trajectory() tracks transition entropy over time: it forms the transitions within each actor's sequence of an event log, pools them in time order, and slides a window of a fixed number of transitions across the stream, giving one entropy estimate per window. A group column gives one trajectory per group. This turns transition entropy from a snapshot into a process measure, as Krejtz et al. (2025) do when they track gaze transition entropy through the phases of a task.

A falling trajectory means the transitions become more predictable (routinisation), a rising one less predictable (exploration), and a level shift marks a change of phase. Each window's estimate rests on window transitions, and with the default step neighbouring windows share four fifths of them, so their estimates are not independent: read the smoothed trend of plot() rather than single windows. For the whole-process value with credible intervals, use transition_entropy() and entropy_bayes().

Usage

entropy_trajectory(
  data,
  action = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  window = 500L,
  step = NULL,
  base = 2
)

# S3 method for class 'net_entropy_trajectory'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_entropy_trajectory'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_entropy_trajectory'
plot(
  x,
  normalized = FALSE,
  span = 0.4,
  title = "Transition entropy over time",
  iter = 200L,
  ci_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

An event log (a data frame with one row per event, read with action), or sequences: a network built from sequences (a netobject, a grouped netobject_group, a tna model), prepared data, or a wide table or character matrix with one row per sequence and one column per position. Sequences are read in position order: each row is one actor, the position is the time, and the groups of a netobject_group become group. A network whose data are not sequences of states (an association or one-hot network) raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

action

The column of an event log holding each event's state. Default NULL, which reads data as sequences.

actor

The column identifying sequences: transitions are formed only between consecutive events of the same actor (within the same group). Default NULL, which reads the data as one sequence.

time

The timestamp column, which orders the events within each actor and places the windows on a time axis. Default NULL, which keeps the row order and uses the row number of the event that ends each transition as the axis. The column must be numeric, a Date or a POSIXct; a character timestamp fails, so parse it first.

group

A column splitting the data into parallel trajectories (for example a condition or an achievement level), each with its own windows. Default NULL (one trajectory, labelled "all"). A missing value in it raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

window

The number of transitions per window, at least 10. Default 500.

step

The number of transitions between the starts of consecutive windows. Default NULL, which uses window %/% 5 (at least 1).

base

The logarithm base, which sets the unit: 2 (default) for bits. Any finite number greater than 1; another value raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

x

For the print() and plot() methods: an entropy_trajectory() result.

digits

For print(): decimal places of the entropies. Default 3.

...

For the print(), summary() and plot() methods: not used.

object

For summary(): an entropy_trajectory() result.

normalized

For plot(): whether to draw entropy_norm instead of the raw entropy. Default FALSE.

span

For plot(): the loess span of the trend line. Default 0.4. A group gets a trend line when span times its number of windows is at least 4 (10 windows at the default); a group with fewer windows is drawn as its windows joined by a line, with a nestimate_sparse_trajectory warning naming it. A group with enough windows whose loess fit still warns is drawn the same way, with a nestimate_trend_not_fitted warning giving loess's message.

title

For plot(): the plot title. Default "Transition entropy over time".

iter

For plot(): the number of bootstrap resamples behind the confidence band of each trend. Default 200; 0 draws the trends without a band.

ci_level

For plot(): the coverage of the band. Default 0.95.

seed

For plot(): a seed for the resampling. It applies to this call only: the session's random state is restored afterwards. Default NULL.

Value

A net_entropy_trajectory object. print() shows each group's number of windows and its mean and range of entropy, and returns its input invisibly. summary() returns a data frame with one row per group: group, windows, the mean, sd, min and max of the window entropies, the entropy of the first and last windows, and their difference change (negative when the transitions became more predictable). plot() returns a ggplot with a loess-smoothed trend per group and its bootstrap confidence band, each group in an Okabe-Ito colour that no state uses and named at the end of its trend; more groups than those colours are drawn one panel each. The object's fields:

trajectory

Data frame, one row per window: group, window (index within the group), time (the window's midpoint; a row number when there is no time column), time_start and time_end (the time, or row number, of the window's first and last transition), n_transitions, n_states (distinct states in the window), entropy (in base units per transition) and entropy_norm (divided by \(\log_b\) of the window's number of states, floored at 2 states so the ceiling is never zero; in \([0, 1]\)).

window, step, base

The settings used.

states

The states of the whole log.

stream

The transitions in time order within each group (state codes, time, group and actor), from which plot() resamples.

state_palette

The colours of the states (the input network's own, or Okabe-Ito dealt over the sorted states). plot() draws the groups in the Okabe-Ito colours these leave, so a group never takes a state's colour.

Details

Each window's entropy is the empirical conditional entropy \(-\sum_{ij} (n_{ij}/N) \log_b(n_{ij}/n_{i\cdot})\), which weights rows by their observed occupancy rather than by the stationary distribution from the eigenvector. Within a short window the chain is often not ergodic (absorbing fragments, unvisited states), where that eigenvector is undefined or misleading; the empirical estimator is the standard windowed choice and converges to the stationary entropy rate over long stationary stretches.

The transitions of all actors are pooled in time order within each group (ties broken by actor, then by input order). A window shorter than window at the end of a stream is dropped; a group whose stream is shorter than window gets one window covering all of it, with a warning. Fewer than two transitions in all raise an error.

The band of plot() is a bootstrap over actors (Davison & Hinkley, 1997): each resample draws a group's actors with replacement, rebuilds its windows from their transitions in time order and fits the same loess trend. The band is the basic bootstrap interval of the trend at each time: the central ci_level of the resampled trends, reflected about the observed trend. It takes the spread of the resampled trends around the observed one as the spread of the observed trend around the true one, so a systematic shift of the resamples is carried to the other side of the trend rather than kept. The plug-in entropy of a window is biased downward (Miller, 1955), by about \((c - r) / (2N \ln b)\) for \(c\) observed transition types from \(r\) states in \(N\) transitions, and resampled actors (repeated transitions) shift it further down, so percentile limits tend to sit below the trend. In a simulation (40 datasets of 100 actors with 20 steps of a stationary 4-state chain, window = 300, step = 100) the 95% band covered the true entropy rate at mid-study in 38 of the 40, missing once on each side. Whole actors are resampled because the windows overlap (each transition sits in about window / step of them) and an actor's transitions depend on each other, so a band from the loess standard error, which treats the windows as independent, would be too narrow. A resample whose trend cannot be fitted (too few windows, or a loess warning) is left out of the band, and the plot warns how many were, with class nestimate_dropped_resamples; a time reached by fewer than half of the iter resamples has no band. A group with one actor has no band (warning class nestimate_single_actor_band).

References

Krejtz, K., Hughes, C.J., Stasiak, I., Duchowski, A., & Krejtz, I. (2025). Real-Time Mobile Transition Matrix Entropy Based on Eye and Head Movements. ETRA '25. doi:10.1145/3715669.3723128

Cover, T.M. & Thomas, J.A. (2006). Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed. Wiley.

Davison, A.C. & Hinkley, D.V. (1997). Bootstrap Methods and Their Application. Cambridge University Press.

Miller, G.A. (1955). Note on the bias of information estimates. In H. Quastler (Ed.), Information Theory in Psychology (pp. 95–100). Free Press.

See also

transition_entropy for the whole-process snapshot, entropy_bayes for credible intervals on it.

Examples

tr <- entropy_trajectory(group_regulation_long,
                         action = "Action", actor = "Actor",
                         time = "Time", group = "Achiever")
tr
#> Entropy Trajectory (9 states; window 500 transitions, step 100)
#> 
#>   High:        123 windows   mean 2.286   range [2.175, 2.394]
#>   Low:         124 windows   mean 2.294   range [2.143, 2.437]
#> 
#> Use plot() for the trajectory, summary() for per-group statistics.
summary(tr)
#>   group windows     mean         sd      min      max    first     last
#> 1  High     123 2.285872 0.04313978 2.175275 2.394429 2.309764 2.301800
#> 2   Low     124 2.294082 0.05803398 2.142537 2.436502 2.233659 2.347734
#>         change
#> 1 -0.007963838
#> 2  0.114074796
plot(tr)


# sequences: the network of the engagement trajectories, by course
net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
entropy_trajectory(net, window = 300, step = 50)
#> Entropy Trajectory (3 states; window 300 transitions, step 50)
#> 
#>   all:          29 windows   mean 1.212   range [1.034, 1.352]
#> 
#> Use plot() for the trajectory, summary() for per-group statistics.
